encounters.cc: Worsening facial acne over 6 months that has not responded to topical treatments, with deep painful nodules along the jawline

lines: Worsening facial acne over 6 months that has not responded to topical treatments, with deep painful nodules along the jawline
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of worsening facial acne that has not responded to topical treatments.
She reports having deep, painful nodules along her jawline and cheeks.
She also mentions that her menstrual cycles have been irregular, occurring every 2-3 months, since menarche at age 13.
- Maternal cousin with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Occupation: Graduate student in Exercise Physiology.
Body mass index (BMI) of 32 kg/m^2. Her blood pressure is 128/82 mmHg.
On examination, you note several large, erythematous nodules on her face, some with visible pus.
She has hirsutism, with excess hair growth on her upper lip and chin.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows multiple small peripheral cysts in both ovaries.

encounters.cc: Concerns about excessive coarse, dark hair growth on upper lip, chin, chest, and back developing over the past year

lines: Concerns about excessive coarse, dark hair growth on upper lip, chin, chest, and back developing over the past year
This 23-year-old female with polycystic ovary syndrome and functional hypothalamic amenorrhea presents with concerns about hair growth.
She reports that over the past year, she has noticed a significant increase in coarse, dark hair on her upper lip, chin, chest, and back.
She denies any changes in her voice or menstrual irregularities.
She is not taking any medications
- Maternal cousin with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Occupation: Graduate student in Exercise Physiology.
On physical examination, you note the presence of terminal hair in a male distribution pattern.
Her BMI is 22 kg/m^2, and the rest of the examination is normal.

encounters.cc: Concerns about irregular menstrual cycles and frustrated weight loss efforts despite diet and exercise

lines: Concerns about irregular menstrual cycles and frustrated weight loss efforts despite diet and exercise
The patient returns for follow-up of polycystic ovary syndrome and functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, having previously presented with refractory facial acne and progressive hirsutism.
She notes that her cycles have never been consistent and often skip several months between periods.
Over the past year, she has noticed increased hair growth in areas that require frequent removal.
She denies changes in appetite or energy level but mentions that weight loss efforts have been frustrating.
She does not report any breast discharge, vision problems, or significant mood changes.
- Maternal cousin with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Occupation: Graduate student in Exercise Physiology.
On physical examination, she has dark, thickened skin over the back of her neck and scattered coarse hairs on her face.
Laboratory evaluation reveals normal thyroid and pituitary function.
A pelvic imaging study reveals bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple small fluid-filled structures near the surface.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of amenorrhea after significantly increasing training intensity and reducing caloric intake

lines: Six-month history of amenorrhea after significantly increasing training intensity and reducing caloric intake
The patient with polycystic ovary syndrome and history of functional hypothalamic amenorrhea returns with amenorrhea.
She reports that her menstrual periods were regular until she increased her training intensity and reduced her caloric intake in an attempt to improve her performance.
She denies any history of pregnancy.
She is not currently taking any medications
- Maternal cousin with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Occupation: Graduate student in Exercise Physiology.
Vital signs are within normal limits
On physical examination, her BMI is 18.5, and she appears fit but thin.
DEXA scan: T-score -2.0 at the lumbar spine

encounters.cc: Worsening hirsutism and persistent acne unresponsive to treatment, with irregular menstrual cycles

lines: Worsening hirsutism and persistent acne unresponsive to treatment, with irregular menstrual cycles
The patient returns to endocrinology with known polycystic ovary syndrome and functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, having previously presented for hirsutism, acne, and menstrual irregularities.
She reports a 6-month history of worsening hirsutism and persistent acne unresponsive to topical treatments, as well as irregular menstrual cycles with her last period occurring 2 months ago.
She denies any significant medical history.
She is not currently taking any medications
- Maternal cousin with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Occupation: Graduate student in Exercise Physiology.
On physical examination, she has an increased distribution of facial hair, acne on her face and upper back.

encounters.cc: Evaluation of absent menses that gradually became spaced out and stopped completely over the past year

lines: Evaluation of absent menses that gradually became spaced out and stopped completely over the past year
The patient with polycystic ovary syndrome and prior amenorrhea following intensified training returns for evaluation.
She reports that she had regular monthly periods until about one year ago when her cycles gradually became more spaced out and eventually stopped.
She denies pregnancy and is not breastfeeding.
No family history of early menopause
She maintains a healthy diet, exercises 2–3 times a week, and has not experienced significant weight loss or gain.
She does not use hormonal contraception.
She is sexually active and uses barrier contraception.
On examination, she appears well-nourished with normal secondary sexual characteristics.
Pelvic examination reveals a normal-appearing cervix and uterus.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
Laboratory evaluation shows normal thyroid function and prolactin levels.
Her serum estradiol is within the normal range, and FSH and LH are in the low-normal range.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a normal-sized uterus and a thin endometrial stripe.
One week later, the patient calls to report the onset of vaginal bleeding.
The clinician administers a 10-day course of oral medroxyprogesterone.

encounters.cc: Irregular periods for the past 6 months with occasional clear discharge from both nipples

lines: Irregular periods for the past 6 months with occasional clear discharge from both nipples
The patient returns to endocrinology for evaluation of menstrual irregularities in the context of her known polycystic ovary syndrome and history of functional hypothalamic amenorrhea.
She has occasional clear discharge from both nipples.
- Maternal cousin with congenital adrenal hyperplasia
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
She runs three times weekly for 30 minutes and does resistance weight training twice per week.
MRI of the brain shows an abnormal mass above the sella turcica.

encounters.cc: Six-month history of rapidly increasing facial hair, deepening voice, bitemporal hair thinning, and cessation of menses

lines: Six-month history of rapidly increasing facial hair, deepening voice, bitemporal hair thinning, and cessation of menses
This 27-year-old female with polycystic ovary syndrome and functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, previously evaluated for hirsutism and amenorrhea, returns with progressive symptoms.
She presents with a 6-month history of increasing facial hair, deepening of her voice, and cessation of her menstrual periods.
She reports significant bitemporal hair thinning and has become increasingly concerned about her physical appearance.
She denies any use of anabolic steroids or other medications.
She has no family history of endocrine disorders
Occupation: Graduate student in Exercise Physiology.
Her blood pressure and other vital signs are within normal limits
On physical examination, she has increased muscle mass, clitoromegaly, and a palpable mass in the lower abdomen.
- Total testosterone: 250 ng/dL (normal female range: 15-70 ng/dL)
An ultrasound of the pelvis shows a 7 cm solid mass in the left ovary.
